{{nihongo|'''Murayama Shrine'''|村山神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iyo Province]].

'''Murayama Shrine''' (むらやまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Doi-chō Tsune, {{ill|Shikokuchūō|Q838666|qid=Q838666}}, {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|Q123376|qid=Q123376}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and its former rank in the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The main deity is {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu-kōdaijin}}. {{ill|Empress Kōgyoku|Q235296|qid=Q235296}}, {{ill|Emperor Tenji|Q314802|qid=Q314802}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}} are additionally enshrined.

=== Overview ===
Since shrine buildings and old records were burned in war fire in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 13 ({{ill|1585|Q6736|qid=Q6736}}), the founding period is unknown. According to shrine tradition, Empress Saimei and Emperor Tenji were merged here in September of {{ill|Hakuhō|Q11580612|qid=Q11580612}} 3 ({{ill|674|Q30302|qid=Q30302}}).

The shrine precinct is said to be the site of Iwase no Angū in Na-ōtsu, where Empress Saimei stayed while heading to Tsukushi to aid Baekje. There are also over 70 wooden statues, said to be attendants of Empress Saimei. A tradition also treats the "Otakarazuka" mound before the shrine as a mausoleum of a noble person.

Generally, Na-ōtsu is identified with Hakata Bay and Iwase no Angū with Miyake in Minami-ku, Fukuoka City. However, this shrine's origin account cites a passage in the '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}' saying "the imperial ship '''returned to''' Na-ōtsu and stayed at Iwase Angū," arguing that Empress Saimei returned by ship eastward from Iyu no Yukata ({{ill|Dōgo Onsen|Q1037748|qid=Q1037748}}) in Iyo and stayed at this site.

In {{ill|Ninju|Q1373077|qid=Q1373077}} 3 {{ill|853|Q30367|qid=Q30367}}, it was included in the myōjin festival. In {{ill|Jōgan|de|Jōgan|es|Jōgan|fa|جوگان|fr|Ère Jōgan|ia|Jogan|id|Jōgan|ja|貞観 (日本)|ko|조간 (연호)|ru|Дзёган|simple|Jōgan|sr|Џоган|tr|Jōgan|uk|Дзьоґан (ненґо)|zh|貞觀 (日本)|zh_yue|貞觀 (日本)|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 9 ({{ill|867|Q30347|qid=Q30347}}) it rose to Junior Fifth Rank Lower, and in Jōgan 12 ({{ill|870|Q23629|qid=Q23629}}) to Junior Fifth Rank Upper. In the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} it is listed as {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}.

It is said that in former times pilgrimage to {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}} was called upper pilgrimage and worship at Murayama Shrine lower pilgrimage, and people from the thirty-three provinces of western Japan substituted worship at Murayama Shrine for pilgrimage to Ise.

It was revered by the {{ill|Kōno clan|Q11554232|qid=Q11554232}} and the Matsudaira lords of {{ill|Saijō Domain|Q2212226|qid=Q2212226}}, and in the Edo period was one of six prayer shrines of Saijō Domain together with {{ill|Isono Shrine|Q11379396|qid=Q11379396}} and others.
